content.title: WHY YOUR {{EYES}} KEEP TELLING ON YOU
facts: **Night blindness** – Struggling to see in dim light or when headlights hit you while driving often points to low vitamin A.
**White spots on skin** – Patchy, pale areas that don't tan can signal low vitamin E or an underlying nutrient absorption issue.
**Cracked corners of the mouth** – Painful splits at the edges of your lips are a classic sign of low riboflavin (B2) or iron.
**Muscle cramps that won't quit** – Calf cramps at night or random muscle spasms often trace back to low magnesium or calcium.
**Tingling or numbness in hands** – A pins-and-needles feeling, especially paired with brain fog, points to low vitamin B12.
**Heart palpitations** – A fluttering or pounding heartbeat with no clear cause can be linked to low potassium or magnesium.
**Dry, scaly patches on the scalp** – Flaky skin that won't go away with regular shampoo can mean low omega-3 or zinc.
**Slow thinking and brain fog** – Feeling mentally slower than usual, even after sleep, is tied to low iron or folate affecting oxygen flow to the brain.

content.caption:
If you've been dealing with night blindness, it might not just be 'bad eyes' — vitamin A is essential for the light-sensitive cells in your retina, and without enough of it those cells can't adapt fast enough when lighting changes. Tingling in your hands is another one worth paying attention to: vitamin B12 is required to maintain the protective coating around your nerves, so when levels drop, nerve signals literally start misfiring. And those heart palpitations that seem to come out of nowhere? Potassium helps regulate the electrical signals that keep your heartbeat steady, so even a mild dip can make your heart feel like it's skipping or racing. Everyone's body is different, so listen to yours and don't ignore patterns that keep repeating.
